body:
### Module

mini.files

### Description

On Windows, `mini.files` appears to use `C://...` as an internal normalized path form. That can be useful internally, but the same path currently reaches the LSP file-operation flow and breaks per-client file-operation filtering.

In the current implementation, rename actions eventually call `vim.uri_from_fname(d.from)` / `vim.uri_from_fname(d.to)` inside the LSP hook. If `d.from` / `d.to` are Windows paths in mini.files' internal `C://Users/...` form, Neovim produces URIs like `file:///C://Users/...`.

Later, `mini.files` applies each client's `workspace.fileOperations.*.filters` by converting the URI back with `vim.uri_to_fname(...):gsub('\\', '/')`. On Windows this remains `C://Users/...`, which does not match lua_ls' normal filter glob such as `C:/Users/Miku/AppData/Local/nvim/**`.

As a result, `mini.files` sends `workspace/didRenameFiles` with `files = {}`. lua_ls receives an empty rename list, so its require-path update logic exits early and the expected "Do you want to modify the require path?" prompt never appears.

### Minimal reproduction / evidence

Environment:

- Windows
- Neovim 0.12.3
- mini.nvim main at `1345d191bb3da9c7b0e977f4387c5761f9bff68d`
- lua-language-server attached to a Lua project rooted at `C:/Users/Miku/AppData/Local/nvim`

Observed from `MiniFilesActionRename` event data:

```lua
from = "C://Users/Miku/AppData/Local/nvim/lua/ray/utils/windows.lua"
to = "C://Users/Miku/AppData/Local/nvim/lua/ray/utils/jindows.lua"
```

Local checks inside Neovim:

```lua
local p = "C://Users/Miku/AppData/Local/nvim/lua/ray/utils/windows.lua"
print(vim.fs.normalize(p))
-- C:/Users/Miku/AppData/Local/nvim/lua/ray/utils/windows.lua

print(vim.uri_from_fname(p))
-- file:///C://Users/Miku/AppData/Local/nvim/lua/ray/utils/windows.lua

print((vim.uri_to_fname(vim.uri_from_fname(p)):gsub('\\', '/')))
-- C://Users/Miku/AppData/Local/nvim/lua/ray/utils/windows.lua
```

Filter match check:

```lua
local glob = "C:/Users/Miku/AppData/Local/nvim/**"
local lp = vim.glob.to_lpeg(glob)

print(lp:match("C:/Users/Miku/AppData/Local/nvim/lua/ray/utils/windows.lua") ~= nil)
-- true

print(lp:match("C://Users/Miku/AppData/Local/nvim/lua/ray/utils/windows.lua") ~= nil)
-- false
```

A control workaround using normalized paths triggers lua_ls correctly:

```lua
Snacks.rename.on_rename_file(vim.fs.normalize(event.data.from), vim.fs.normalize(event.data.to))
```

That causes lua_ls to show the expected Modify Require Path prompt.

### Expected behavior

`mini.files` may keep `C://...` internally if needed, but paths should be normalized/canonicalized before crossing the LSP boundary. In particular, LSP URI construction and file-operation filter matching should use canonical Windows paths like `C:/Users/...`, not mini.files' internal `C://Users/...` representation.

### Related context

- LSP file-operation support was added in #2340.
- Windows path normalization behavior is related to #2277.
- I could not find an existing issue connecting the Windows `C://` internal path form with LSP file-operation filtering producing empty `files` arrays.

comment_data.body: Sorry guys, I asked the agent to investigate this issue, but unexpectedly it directly created an issue using gh cli 😅 I'll create one by hand later

> I'll create one by hand later

Please do and if it'll happen, please provide a real reproduction steps like "Create these files with these contents, open them, enable certain LSP server (important to note which one), open 'mini.files', rename this file to this name, observe the problem".

But as far as I remember, @TheLeoP did do extra tests on Windows to make sure LSP integration worked there too.

The explanation of the AI doesn't make a lot of sense, but yes, there seems to be a problem with the LSP integration in Windows.

https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/bf8169f3e518be8de3f88073ace37d91f576cb04/lua/mini/files.lua#L2704-L2709

Normalizes all Windows paths to `C://` (because of #2272). `lua_ls` always sends globs starting with `C:/`, so they never match for any path.

On top of that, notifying `lua_ls` about files starting with `C://` results on it not recognizing them and, in turn, not asking Neovim to do any further modifications. So, simply changing `C://` to `C:/` for the filter check 

https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/bf8169f3e518be8de3f88073ace37d91f576cb04/lua/mini/files.lua#L2873

is not enough.

I guess that the more robust solution would be "de-normalizing" files when first converting them to URIs on 

https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/bf8169f3e518be8de3f88073ace37d91f576cb04/lua/mini/files.lua#L2844-L2846

Something like 


```lua
  local files, to_uri =
    {},
    H.is_windows and function(x) return vim.uri_from_fname(x:gsub('^(%a)://([^/])', '%1:/%2')) end or vim.uri_from_fname
```

```diff
diff --git a/lua/mini/files.lua b/lua/mini/files.lua
index 43bcaf8..9037fc7 100644
--- a/lua/mini/files.lua
+++ b/lua/mini/files.lua
@@ -2835,7 +2835,9 @@ H.lsp_fs_hook = function(method, diffs, lsp_timeout)
   -- https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#createFilesParams
   -- https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#deleteFilesParams
   -- https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#renameFilesParams
-  local files, to_uri = {}, vim.uri_from_fname
+  local files, to_uri =
+    {},
+    H.is_windows and function(x) return vim.uri_from_fname(x:gsub('^(%a)://([^/])', '%1:/%2')) end or vim.uri_from_fname
   local needs_check = method == 'willCreate' or method == 'willRename'
   local is_create, is_delete, is_rename =
     vim.endswith(method, 'Create'), vim.endswith(method, 'Delete'), vim.endswith(method, 'Rename')
```

---

This wasn't caught by our tests on Windows because they were expecting to see `C://`. It wasn't caught by me because I knew `\\` had issues with globs, I didn't know that `C://` was also problematic :p

> On top of that, notifying lua_ls about files starting with C:// results on it not recognizing them and, in turn, not asking Neovim to do any further modifications. So, simply changing C:// to C:/ for the filter check

There are two important questions here:
- Is it only `lua_ls` thing? I.e. does this reproduce on other (reputable) LSP servers?
- Is there anything in the LSP specification about this case? I'd guess not, but still worth double checking.

@TheLeoP Thanks for your investigation! I was just trying to create a minimal reproduction of lua_ls, but it seems like I don't need to do that anymore 🫣

@echasnovski I tested this in a rust project and a typescript project, and yes, lsps automatically update their import paths

> @echasnovski I tested this in a rust project and a typescript project, and yes, lsps automatically update their import paths

Thanks for the follow up!

Then unless there is an easy and non-invasive way of fixing this in 'mini.files', I'd be comfortable to say that this is a known LuaLS limitation. With later opening an issue there about this.

I am also curious about whether `emmylua_ls` works here.

I investigated further, and it seems this is indeed an implementation issue with lua_ls - lua_ls defines [a glob with a working directory path](https://github.com/LuaLS/lua-language-server/blob/master/script/provider/provider.lua#L201); while [vtsls](https://github.com/yioneko/vtsls/blob/main/packages/server/src/capabilities.ts#L92-L99) and [rust-analyzer](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust-analyzer/blob/master/crates/rust-analyzer/src/lsp/capabilities.rs#L114-L122) use less stricter ones. However, neo-tree previously integrated well with `Snacks.rename.on_rename_file`, so I think the internal non-standard windows paths being passed to lsp might be an issue we can fix here
@TheLeoP, could you please take a look and confirm that this is mostly (only?) a problem of `LuaLS`? In particular, is there such issue for `emmylua_ls`?

It seems that `lua_ls` is not the only LSP with issues when using paths in the `C://` form (instead of `C:/`):

- `lua_ls`: globs never match. Even if they did, files in the `C://` form are ignored by it
- `tsgo`: files in the `C://` form are ignored

On the other hand, not all language servers had this issue

- `basedpyright` worked just fine
- `emmylua_ls` worked just fine

So... it seems like this could be marked as an issue on the language server side (?

---

I think that it should be reasonable to do something about **all** globs that are an absolute path never matching on Windows because of `C://`. It wouldn't solve the issue either for `lua_ls` nor `tsgo`, but it would mean that "everything is working as it should" on `mini.files` side.

1. This diff fixes absolute glob matching on Windows, but does not fix the issue with `lua_ls` and `tsgo`.

```diff
diff --git a/lua/mini/files.lua b/lua/mini/files.lua
index 0bdf1fa..ca91033 100644
--- a/lua/mini/files.lua
+++ b/lua/mini/files.lua
@@ -2865,10 +2865,13 @@ H.lsp_fs_hook_client = function(client, full_method, lsp_files, timeout)
     local adjust_case = ignore_case and vim.fn.tolower or function(x) return x end
     -- On Windows `uri_to_fname` forces `\`, but forcing / seems more robust
     local to_fname = H.is_windows and function(x) return (vim.uri_to_fname(x):gsub('\\', '/')) end or vim.uri_to_fname
+    -- On Windows absolute globs never match paths starting with `C://`, so `C:/` is forced
+    local normalize_for_glob = H.is_windows and function(x) return x:gsub('^(%a)://([^/])', '%1:/%2') end
+      or function(x) return x end
     local glob_lpeg = vim.glob.to_lpeg(adjust_case(glob) or '**')
     return function(lsp_file)
       local uri = lsp_file.uri or lsp_file.oldUri
-      local fname = adjust_case(to_fname(uri))
+      local fname = normalize_for_glob(adjust_case(to_fname(uri)))
       return is_scheme(uri, scheme) and is_fs_type(lsp_file, ref_fs_type) and glob_lpeg:match(fname) ~= nil
     end
   end
```

After applying this diff, `lua_ls` gets a notification that looks like

```
┆H.lsp_fs_hook_client┆ ╎params╎ ┊1┊: {
  files = { {
      newUri = "file:///C://Users/luis/Desktop/test/b.lua",
      oldUri = "file:///C://Users/luis/Desktop/test/b_algo.lua"
    } }
}
```

and decides to ignore it because of the `C://`. Before applying the diff, no notification was sent.

2. This diff fixes absolute glob matching in Windows **and** the issue with `lua_ls`/`tsgo`.

```diff
diff --git a/lua/mini/files.lua b/lua/mini/files.lua
index 0bdf1fa..4b6c974 100644
--- a/lua/mini/files.lua
+++ b/lua/mini/files.lua
@@ -2829,7 +2829,11 @@ H.lsp_fs_hook = function(method, diffs, lsp_timeout)
   -- https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#createFilesParams
   -- https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#deleteFilesParams
   -- https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#renameFilesParams
-  local files, to_uri = {}, vim.uri_from_fname
+  local files, to_uri =
+    {},
+    -- On Windows we normalize paths to `C://` which works on Neovim but has issues for absolute globs matching and
+    -- some Language Server implementations. So, `C:/` is forced
+    H.is_windows and function(x) return vim.uri_from_fname(x:gsub('^(%a)://([^/])', '%1:/%2')) end or vim.uri_from_fname
   local needs_check = method == 'willCreate' or method == 'willRename'
   local is_create, is_delete, is_rename =
     vim.endswith(method, 'Create'), vim.endswith(method, 'Delete'), vim.endswith(method, 'Rename')
```

After applying this diff, `lua_ls` gets a notification that looks like

```
┆H.lsp_fs_hook_client┆ ╎params╎ ┊1┊: {
  files = { {
      newUri = "file:///C:/Users/luis/Desktop/test/b_algo.lua",
      oldUri = "file:///C:/Users/luis/Desktop/test/b.lua"
    } }
}
```

and asks Neovim to update the imports accordingly.

> 2\. This diff fixes absolute glob matching in Windows **and** the issue with `lua_ls`/`tsgo`.

Okay, it seems that dedicated wrappers around `vim.uri_to_fname` and `vim.uri_from_fname` are in order. Since there is also a `local to_fname` that needs tweaks on Windows.

The tip of the [`backlog`](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/tree/backlog) branch should contain the fix for this issue. @TheLeoP and @so1ve, could you please test that it works as expected?

> Can confirm this works 👍

Thanks! This should now be part of the latest `main`. Let's hope these changes have no unintended side effects :)
Sorry for the delay, I can also confirm that the fix works as expected. Thanks, echa!

title: mini.files: Windows C:// internal paths break LSP file operation filters
